text:
maria: heads-up — after the kernel-selector change in the s/seq-gating PR we see a small but consistent p99 regression for long sequences (3k-6k) on H100 pools. not huge (5-7%) but reproducible in canary. :eyes:
raj: saw that in traces too. appears only when tile_size=128 path gets chosen. if we force tile=192 the p99 drops back. suspect occupancy + register spill interplay.
lin: can you paste the nsight/nvprof snippet? curious about regs/shared usage and active blocks per SM.
maria: pasted profiler excerpt below (trimmed):
```
Kernel: kv_tile_loop_prefetch
GPU: H100
gridDim=(1024,1,1) blockDim=(256,1,1)
regsPerThread=62 sharedMemPerBlock=2176B
activeBlocksPerSM=2 achieved_occupancy=0.35
local_mem_spills=12MB total_spill_count=384
L1_hit_rate=0.73 smem_bandwidth=85GB/s
```
raj: 62 regs/thread on H100 with block=256 is pretty high. that reduces occupancy a lot. tile=192 path uses block=192 and regs/thread=52 in our tuning; occupancy jumps to ~0.5.
oren: but switching to larger tile increases shared usage per block which can reduce active blocks. we need to balance reg pressure vs smem per-block. also KV-prefetch path copies ~12KB per block into shared which constrains tiling.
lin: proposal: make kernel-picker autotuner aware of two extra dims: (regs, smem) and select the candidate with highest effective_throughput = occupancy * (threads_per_block) * throughput_coeff(arch). do a quick empirical coeff per-arch. we already sample single-seq perf for each option.
maria: i like that. immediate quick fix: add seq_len buckets -> prefer tile=192 for seq_len >= 2048, fallback to 128 below. should reduce p99 until autotune lands.
benchbot: quick microbench results (canary H100, model=redwood-v1, batch=1):
```
./bench --model redwood-v1 --seq 4096 --batch 1 --tile 128
p50=120ms p95=210ms p99=285ms
./bench --model redwood-v1 --seq 4096 --batch 1 --tile 192
p50=110ms p95=195ms p99=265ms
```
raj: that matches. ~7% p99 drop when forcing tile 192. but on A100 we saw the opposite for mid-seq (1k-2k) because regs behave differently. need arch-aware mapping.
lin: action plan: (1) raj run a small grid sweep per-arch (A100/H100) for seq buckets [256,512,1024,2048,4096] across tile sizes [96,128,160,192], block sizes [128,192,256], collect regs/smem/occupancy and effective throughput. (2) oren add a quick runtime guard: per-request choose path based on seq bucket + arch lookup table. (3) maria revert canary if we hit >6% p99 regression in stable.
oren: note on KV cache behavior: higher tiles increase prefix reuse and cache hit rate for short prefixes, but they hurt when user requests have lots of unique prefixes (chat sessions) because smem copy time grows. we should instrument kv_hit_ratio in the canary traces.
maria: added instrumentation ticket in #incidents, will attach traces.
benchbot: queued autotune sweep job: tune-2237654321-001 (will post results to /tmp/autotune/2237654321). estimated runtime 2h.
deploy-bot: canary rollout paused at 60% on H100 region due to anomaly detector (p99_delta > 4%). :pause_button:
raj: while autotune runs, I'll implement the seq-bucket quick fix and a small perf counter that logs regsPerThread and sharedMemPerBlock for chosen kernel at runtime. cheap to add.
lin: keep an eye on register_spill_count metric — if it rises >10% on a path we should disable that path and prefer a lower-reg kernel.
maria: thanks all. please drop results in this thread. if autotune shows per-arch differences we should check adding arch-specific default profiles in kernel-catalog. :thumbsup:
